title: Sitting in at Jazzland and getting music first on the boat
summary: He and Pops Foster sat in at an open-air club and handled a trick tune change, because the boat got new music before others.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Do you remember anything about Jazzland, what it was like? Did you ever go there and sit in?

Well, yes. I went there and sit in with the band one night. Turpin had given a macaroni dinner for the Bullock band. And we went on out there. And the guys in the band, at least a piano player in the band, he was rated as the best blues player in St. Louis. I just remember his name. I think his name was John something. And the Russian racket just came out. It was kind of a tough number. So what he done was Pat Foster and I was in the band. Dodge was sitting in the band. And he called Indian Blues. It must have been a made up plot against Pat Foster and I, you see. He called Indian Blues and the band struck the introduction of Russian Rag.
Oh yeah, that's a tough precaution.

We had been playing Russian Rag on the boat for about six weeks, you see. And we missed two measures because we was starting on Indian Blues, you see. But after we played the, we went da da da, da da, da da, da, da, da, da, da. We came right on in, we knew what he was playing.

We were familiar with the number, we got the number on the boat before they got it. Because Captain Joe, they used to send Captain Joe music by the month. They sent him a stack of music and they'd bill him for it, you see. So we used to get music first. The boats used to get music first. So when the other guys got it, we'd be playing in about three weeks.
What kind of a place was it? Was it a big dance hall?
No, but it was just an open yard.
I did hear something about being at Kent there one time, too. Do you remember any Kent over there?

No, not at the time I was there. Not around 1918, 1919. Must have been later. It was just no open yard. And the music stand was on the side. It was covered. It was the only place covered. All the rest was out in the open.
